findings.message: The seeded fixture entity uses a hand-written id ('e-fixture', cast through `as unknown as Entity`) instead of the deterministic id. The other new tests in this Story that seed the store (scope-area, docs-scope, docs-area-retrieval, dropped-or-failed) build it with makeEntityId(repo, file, kind, name).
Same as live-runs.test.ts: the seeded fixture entity uses the literal id 'e-fixture' rather than makeEntityId(repo, file, kind, name).

The `Fixture` interface declares its optional properties `registry?` (line 31) and `indexed?` (line 33) without the explicit `| undefined`. The production types added in this Story (AbsentInput, FailedTask.code, DataScope.connectionId, the `area?` args) do spell it out.

The two new tests load modules with `await import(...)` inside the test body ('../../context/invariants.js', '../cache.js', 'node:fs', 'node:url'). The new sibling test files (walker-aggregate, walker-walk-failure) import the same kinds of module statically at the top. Nothing here needs lazy loading, so this departs from the module's static, `.js`-suffixed top-of-file import layout.
findings.expectationRef: module-idiom: static top-of-file imports in test files

findings.message: The runtime reads its scope into the family-local `ScopeRef` (kind: string) and then casts it with `scopeRef as AnalyzeScopeRef` to call resolveTaskScope. The same cast is repeated in discovery-modules, structure-module-tree, docs/discovery-inventory and the six infra runtimes. The docs constraint, decision and family-summary runtimes and data/_shared pass the already-typed `args.intent.scopeRef` with no cast. Two ways of handing a scope to the one scope function now coexist; an unknown kind is only caught at run time by the table check.
findings.expectationRef: module-idiom: typed scopeRef hand-over to resolveTaskScope

findings.message: Correctness/error-path risk: with an area, the vector search is given `ids: [...candidateById.keys()]`, i.e. every candidate of the area as an id filter. For a large area (a module scope over a docs tree with thousands of sections) this is an unbounded id list pushed into the Lance filter; it can be slow or be rejected. The surrounding try then drops the whole vector pass, so a large area silently falls back to keyword-only ranking while a small one gets vector scores. Nothing in the visible tests covers an area above three candidates.

Correctness risk: when `task.params.scopeRefValue` is present, `resolveDataScope` is skipped entirely, so neither the data row's kind check nor the connection restriction applies. The test confirms that under a `connection` scope (and even a `symbol` scope the data row refuses) the override lists every connection of the overriding path. That contradicts the documented rule in docs/daemon.md that a data task with a connection scope works on that connection alone: a planner-written param lifts the restriction.

Correctness risk in the uncaught-error handler: it writes a failed record under the run id unconditionally from `reached.record`. Nothing refuses a second start under an id whose run is still going (live-runs.ts counts them for that reason), so a run that throws overwrites the shared run.json of the other, still-live run with `failed`/`internal-error`; the live run's later writes then flip it back. The same handler also rewrites a record already written as `ok`/`done` to `failed` if anything throws after the final write, because `reached.stage` keeps the last in-progress stage.

Duplication: `resolveScopeForTarget` re-implements the pairing test inline (`table[target].includes(ref.kind)`) where prepareScope previously called the classifier's own predicate, which this change stops importing. Two expressions of the same rule now exist; a change to the predicate (e.g. special-casing a target) would not reach the scope function.

Duplication: `inDocsArea` is a second directory-or-file containment predicate (equal, or prefix plus '/') next to the area predicate the runtimes use from shared/task-scope.ts, with `DocsArea` produced from a resolved scope by `docsAreaOf`. The inventory and family-summary tasks filter with one, retrieval with the other, so the 'area' of a scope is decided in two places. Both also depend on an un-normalised path: a directory value with a trailing slash matches nothing and returns an empty result without an error.

Error-path inconsistency: `connectionWithinScope` refuses a task that names a connection outside the scope with a plain `Error`. `scopeErrorMapping` does not recognise it, so the walk records it as `runtime-threw: ...` with no `code`, unlike every other scope refusal introduced by this Story, and a client cannot tell it from a crash.

Avoidable work: in `purgeRun`, an abandoned record is rewritten as failed by `abandonRunRecord` and the run directory is then removed in the same call, so the write (and its log line and failure branch) has no observable effect.

Avoidable complexity: the name `writeRunRecord` means two different things in one file. Inside `runStages` it is a shadowing wrapper that also updates `reached`; in `runAnalyze`'s handler it is the raw writer, aliased as `writeRunRecordToDisk` only to make the shadow possible. A write added to the wrong function silently skips, or wrongly applies, the bookkeeping the handler relies on. A distinctly named wrapper would remove the trap.

Test-isolation risk: `_setTaskScopeDepsForTest` is called at module top level and never reset, and the new test calls `_resetRuntimeRegistryForTests()` and registers a single runtime without restoring the built-in registrations. Later tests in the same file that read the registry become order-dependent.

Brittle tests: several new tests assert on source text by regex with exact spelling and spacing (e.g. `const scope\s+= await resolveTaskScope(scopeRef as AnalyzeScopeRef, 'code', TEMPLATE_ID);`, the driver's `finalReport === undefined` block in walker-aggregate.test.ts, the import scan in walker.test.ts). A behaviour-preserving refactor or reformat fails them, and they prove the text is present, not the behaviour.
